definitions.gloss: here and there; scattered; dotted about
definitions.explanation: Describes things distributed sparsely and irregularly across a surface or area, like dots on a canvas.

examples.japanese: {島|しま}が{点々|てんてん}と{浮|う}かんでいる。
examples.english: Islands are scattered across the water.

examples.japanese: {野原|のはら}に{花|はな}が{点々|てんてん}と{咲|さ}いている。
examples.english: Flowers are blooming here and there in the field.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}の{上|うえ}に{動物|どうぶつ}の{足跡|あしあと}が{点々|てんてん}と{続|つづ}いていた。
examples.english: Animal footprints dotted the snow, trailing off into the distance.

notes:
USAGE:
{点々|てんてん}と is an adverb describing things distributed sparsely like dots. It conveys a visual image of items spread out with space between them.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {点々|てんてん}と{散|ち}らばる (to be scattered about)
- {点々|てんてん}と{続|つづ}く (to continue in a dotted line)
- {点々|てんてん}と{浮|う}かぶ (to float here and there)

GRAMMAR:
{点々|てんてん} can also be used as a noun meaning "dots" or "dotted marks." When used with と, it functions as an adverb.
